newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bertelsmann to decide structure this year.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann to decide structure this year.

text.p: A final decision on a planned reorganisation at German media giant Bertelsmann should be taken this year, Mark Woessner, Bertelsmann's managing board chairman, said in an interview published on Monday.

Woessner also told financial daily La Tribune Desfosses that Bertelsmann could well seek a separate stock market quote for certain subsidiaries, notably BMG Entertainment, but said that nothing had yet been decided.
Asked if Bertelsmann would create a holding company to top its four constituent companies in its main sectors of activity, he said there was already Bertelsmann AG to take care of strategy.

"We are looking at all the alternatives so that we can have a more efficient organisation and more rapid decision making, so as to fine-tune the existing system. The final decision should be taken this year," Woessner said.

Asked about bringing certain activities to the stock market, Woessner said: "It is a possible alternative, especially for BMG Entertainment. We are thinking about it. It will depend on strategic opportunities we see in the entertainment market. But nothing has yet been decided and we have no financial need."
He noted that Bertelsmann had financed the merger of its broadcasting unit UFA with Luxemburg's CLT last year from cash flow.
Woessner said the good years in publishing were over in Germany. "There is a plethora of titles and a growing competition for advertising between the press and other media," he said.
Bertelsmann's response consists of investing in new markets and electronic media, he said.

It sees expansion possibilities for its publishing unit, Gruner & Jahr, in the U.S. and in Asia, particularly in China, where it is in the process of creating a book club with a Chinese partner, he said.
In electronic media, he said publishers did not need to fear software companies like Microsoft.

"We don't need to develop a new browser ourselves. But everyone who has one needs us to have content to offer. So I don't think that Microsoft will become the leader of world publishing in the future," he said.
